description: Canonical monorepo layout for company projects

packages.shared-types: Interfaces, DTOs, enums shared by frontend and backend
packages.shared-utils: Utility functions shared by frontend and backend

root.infrastructure: IaC and local/dev container composition (docker-compose, Terraform). NOT Kubernetes deployment manifests — those live in the platform-created deployment-<app> repo at apps/<app>/<env>/.

workspaces.packageManager: Bun workspaces: root package.json `workspaces: ["apps/*", "packages/*"]`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, committed bun.lock. No package-lock.json, yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml.

rootFiles.Dockerfile: The production Dockerfile lives at the REPO ROOT, not under infrastructure/ — the deployment platform's build detects it there. A docker-compose or dev-only Dockerfile may still live under infrastructure/.

legacy: Projects with Vibe Start before 2026-10-07 may keep their existing stack and package manager (npm/pnpm workspaces, React/Vue, Express). Audit them against their existing structure as advisory; do not convert. Adding a module, service, workspace or app is a major improvement and needs tech-architect approval in PROJECT.md `## Stack Exceptions`.
rules: Use Bun workspaces (root package.json `workspaces`) linking apps/* and packages/*; never npm/yarn/pnpm on new projects
Frontend code must live only under apps/frontend
Backend code must live only under apps/backend
Never duplicate interfaces, DTOs, enums, or types between apps — use packages/shared-types
Never duplicate shared utilities — use packages/shared-utils
Prefer importing shared packages over copying code
The production Dockerfile stays at the repo root; do not move it under infrastructure/

Kubernetes deployment manifests never live in the application repo. They are generated by the deployment platform in deployment-<app> at onboarding, so their absence here is correct and is never a structure finding.
